narration: If you've been married, there's a hidden Social Security benefit most people never know about. The average couple misses $400,000 by never claiming it.
visual: Two interlocking wedding rings (SVG circles) on dark background spring into view. Large amber dollar sign and title 'SPOUSAL BENEFIT' fade in below. Subtext: 'The $400K Secret'.

narration: You can claim up to 50% of your partner's Social Security — even if you never worked a day in your life. That's up to $1,900 a month, just for being married.
visual: Social Security card SVG (dark rectangle with amber header reading 'SOCIAL SECURITY') slides in. Dollar amount counter animates from $0 to $1,900/mo. '50% OF SPOUSE' badge appears.

narration: Wild part — it also works if you're divorced. Marriage lasted ten years? You still qualify, your ex is never notified, and their benefit doesn't shrink one dollar.
visual: Calendar SVG springs in showing '10 YEARS'. Scissors SVG slides in from left, symbolizing divorce. Text reveals: 'DIVORCED? YOU STILL QUALIFY'.

narration: But 40% of eligible spouses never claim this benefit. Social Security won't volunteer the information — and that silence costs the average qualifying couple $400,000.
visual: Ten stick-figure people SVGs appear. Four of them grayed out with red X marks (representing 40%). Dollar counter climbs from $0 to $400K. Title: '40% NEVER CLAIM IT'.

narration: Timing matters though. Claim at 62 and you only get 32.5%. Wait until 67 — your full retirement age — and you collect the full 50%. That gap is worth $200,000.
visual: Horizontal timeline bar animating from age 62 to 67. Percentage badge tracks along bar rising from 32.5% to 50%. Labels show 'EARLY' at left, 'FULL' at right.

narration: Check yours for free at ssa.gov — log in and see your statement. If you qualify, this might be the easiest $400,000 decision you ever make. Follow for more moves like this.
visual: Phone SVG displaying 'ssa.gov' screen with a green checkmark and sample benefit amount. CTA button: 'FREE AT SSA.GOV'. Text: 'Follow for more money moves the system won't tell you'.
